title: Operator intervention record
description: One record per correction the operator or an independent check makes to harness output. This is the instrument CLM-0001 needs: it measures whether operator interventions fall while quality holds. It is also the input the pattern-promotion path has never had.

intervention_id.description: INT-YYYYMMDD-NNN. The date is the date of the correction, not of the backfill.

engagement_id.description: Directory name under engagements/, or 'harness' for a correction to the harness itself.

provenance.description: live: captured when the correction happened. backfilled: reconstructed later from a written record. Never mix the two in one statistic without saying so.

stage.description: The stage that produced the wrong claim, not the stage that caught it.

judgement_class.description: What the operator supplied. authorization and taste are the classes least likely to be automatable.

detected_by.description: self means the same actor that made the claim caught it. external-party means a vendor or third party caught it.

latency.description: How long the wrong claim survived. same-round is cheap. Anything later is the expensive class.

claim_before.description: The wrong claim, quoted where possible.

source_refs.description: Where the evidence for this record lives. For a backfilled record this is the file and line that documents the correction. A record with no source cannot be audited.

machine_checkable.description: True when a deterministic check could have caught this claim. This field selects the regression corpus for tools/score-finding.py.

check_shape.description: If machine_checkable, name the check. Example: 'cited path must exist', 'severity vector must recompute'.

check_family.description: The reusable check that would catch this class. `one-off` means the shape needs bespoke domain logic and does NOT generalise. Count families, not shapes: a corpus of 52 unique shapes gives a tool 52 special cases, whereas a corpus of 8 families gives it 8 checks. Only non-`one-off` entries scope tools/score-finding.py.

check_mode.description: computable: a program can decide the claim from the artifacts alone (a path exists, a number recomputes). attestable: a program cannot judge the work, but it can refuse a finding that does not name the required reference (an enumeration census, a negative control, a real-path run). Both are enforceable; only the first is decidable.
